Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Krishna Kant Dubey,Lavkush Dixit

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

By means of this third bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Anuj Kumar, who is involved in Case Crime No. 351 of 2020, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, police station Kishni, district Mainpuri, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

The first and second bail applications of the applicant were rejected vide orders dated 28.07.2021 and 09.01.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 6049 of 2021 and 17431 of 2022 on merits.

sentences.text: Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the applicant has been languishing in jail since 24.08.2020 but till date, his trial has not been concluded on account of slackness on the part of the prosecution, therefore, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that in this case, victim is minor and she has already been examined before the trial Court.
The second bail application of the applicant was rejected considering the statement of the victim given before the trial Court.

So far as delay in concluding the trial of the applicant is concerned, it is argued that, out of 10 prosecution witnesses, 03 prosecution witnesses including the victim have been examined before the trial Court and on 12 dates, case was adjourned on account of delaying tactics adopted by co-accused.
It is also submitted that efforts shall be made to produce remaining prosecution witnesses for early conclusion of the trial.
Hence, bail application of the applicant is liable to be rejected.

Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perusing the order-sheet, I find that vide order dated 07.08.2023, status report of the trial was called for from the concerned Presiding Officer, who in turn, submitted report dated 22.08.2023, which is on record, wherein it is mentioned that statement of the victim was completed on 14.07.2022.
In the meantime, statement of the informant/PW-2 was also recorded on 27.04.2022.
On 17.05.2022, statement of the Investigating Officer Jaikab Fernandez was recorded as PW-3 but no cross-examination was done by the accused Surjan.
Thereafter, notice under Section 350 Cr.P.C. was sent to witnessJaikab Fernandez but he did not appear.
It is also mentioned that on account of death of Presiding Officer in a road accident, Court was vacant upto 29.04.2023.
Lastly, it is mentioned that all efforts are being made to get the trial of the accused concluded.
Under the circumstances of the case as noted above, this Court feels that it would be appropriate to issue direction to concerned Court below to conclude the trial within time-bound period.
Hence, prayer for bail of the applicant is refused.
The bail application is rejected.
It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.

However, the trial Court is directed to make an endeavour to conclude the trial of the applicant expeditiously preferably within a period of nine months from the date of production of a copy of this order without granting any unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri is directed to ensure production of remaining prosecution witnesses before the trial Court on the date fixed.
Registrar (Compliance) and learned Government Advocate of this Court shall communicate this order to the Superintendent of Police, Mainpuri for information and compliance.

Order Date :- 16.1.2024 Shubham  Anuj Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163573266/
